readme:
# 条件路径与速度回归

## 1. 论文解决什么问题

Flow Matching 学习一个随时间变化的速度场，用常微分方程把噪声搬运到数据。条件训练目标允许直接回归可计算的速度，不必在每次训练时模拟整条生成轨迹。

本模块精选线性条件路径及其 CFM 目标。只需实现 `interpolate`、`cfm_target`、`cfm_loss`；时间采样、Euler 求解器、测试模型和训练循环已经提供。

## 2. 核心公式

本题固定 x0 是噪声，x1 是数据。二者均为 `[B,D]`，时间 t 为 `[B]`，每个样本拥有自己的插值比例：

$$x_t=(1-t)x_0+tx_1,\qquad u=x_1-x_0,\qquad\mathcal L=\operatorname{mean}_{b,d}\left(v_\theta(x_t,t)-u\right)^2.$$

条件速度 u 是一对端点之间的位移，但网络只看见当前位置和时间。同一位置可能由不同端点对产生，因此它学到的是条件速度的平均值。即使网络达到最优，训练损失一般仍不为零；不可约方差不等于实现错误。梯度等价性及线性条件路径见 [Flow Matching 式 5、9、22、23](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.02747v2)。

单点数据是特殊情况：$v^*(x,t)=(\mu-x)/(1-t)$，代入插值即可得到恒定目标速度，因此 oracle loss 为零，Euler 一步也能到达数据点。一般混合分布的边缘轨迹会弯曲，多步求解才有意义。

## 3. 从公式到代码

实现三个围绕同一训练目标的函数：

```text
interpolate: 将 t [B] 广播到 [B,...]，构造噪声到数据的线性路径
cfm_target: 返回这条路径对时间的导数
cfm_loss: 在 interpolate 的结果上调用 model(x,t)
将模型速度与 cfm_target 的元素平方误差取平均
```

`interpolate` 和 `cfm_target` 保持端点张量的形状与 dtype。`cfm_loss` 返回一个标量，平均必须覆盖 batch 和所有坐标，并保留模型参数的梯度。

`sample_t` 与 `euler_sample` 已提供。测试 harness 管理模型、优化器和训练循环，训练时会调用你的 `cfm_loss`。默认时间均匀采样；辅助函数里的 logit-normal 选项供后续比较。

## 4. 本题约定

| 项目 | 本模块约定 |
| --- | --- |
| 端点 | `x0` 是噪声，`x1` 是数据 |
| 时间 | `t` 为 `[B]`，从 0 走向 1 |
| 条件路径 | 采用论文条件 OT 路径在终端噪声为零时的形式 |
| 配对 | 独立噪声与数据配对 |
| 损失归约 | 对 batch 及所有坐标取平均 |
| 测试模型 | `model(x,t)` 返回与 x 同形状的速度 |

由条件目标回归学到的是边缘速度场，无需为每个训练样本求解整条 ODE。

## 5. 交互可视化

<viz id="flow_particles" />

播放粒子流动并拖动时间，查看当前位置的速度场箭头。切换 Euler 步数，比较直线 oracle 与学习到的弯曲轨迹。

<viz id="convention_bug" />

切换反向采样错误，观察同一模型如何生成错误结果；同时查看 loss 曲线，理解 loss 下降不足以证明采样正确。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸

提供的 Euler 求解器沿时间递增积分，在左端点求值以避开单点 oracle 的 t=1 奇点：

$$x_{k+1}=x_k+\frac1n v_\theta(x_k,k/n),\quad k=0,\ldots,n-1.$$

可进一步阅读 [Rectified Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03003) 的重新耦合，以及 [SD3 式 13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.03206v1) 的反向时间约定与非均匀时间采样。这些比较属于拓展，不增加本模块的必做函数。
notes:
# 通过后的复盘

- 插值、目标符号、积分方向必须一致。`test_point_zero_loss` 检查训练，`test_gaussian_transport` 与 `test_learns_eight_modes` 检查生成，避免只看 loss 下降。
- 单点 oracle 在 t=1 有奇点；Euler 用左端点求值，最大时间是 (n-1)/n。`test_no_singular_endpoint` 直接记录调用时间。
- 条件目标有不可约方差，CFM loss 通常不能降到零。`test_point_zero_loss` 的特殊单点数据才具有零最优误差；真实训练曲线保留非零终值。
- 本题 loss 是所有 batch 和坐标元素取平均；与对坐标求和再对 batch 平均相差维度因子，`test_reference` 明确这一约定。
- 2000 步 TimeMLP 并非完美 oracle：半径 .5 的离群率实测 .123，阈值按规格规则取 ×1.5=.1845，MMD 也按 ×1.5 标定，并单独要求八模式均覆盖、每模式占比距 .125 不超过 .05。具体环境和数值在 problem.yaml；该阈值针对短训练预算，并不等同 DDPM 反向去噪模块的精确 oracle 质量。

时间方向已核对 [Lipman 式 22–23](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.02747v2)、[Rectified Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03003)、[SD3 式 13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.03206v1)，访问日期 2026-10-13。

en.title: Conditional Path and Velocity Regression
en.readme:
# Conditional Path and Velocity Regression

## 1. What the paper solves

Flow Matching learns a time-dependent velocity field that transports noise into data through an ordinary differential equation. Its conditional training objective regresses a directly computable velocity, without simulating an entire generation trajectory on every training step.

This module selects the linear conditional path and its CFM objective. Implement only `interpolate`, `cfm_target`, and `cfm_loss`; time sampling, the Euler solver, test model, and training loop are supplied.

## 2. Core equations

In this exercise, x0 is noise and x1 is data. Both have shape `[B,D]`; time t has shape `[B]`, with a separate interpolation weight for each sample:

$$x_t=(1-t)x_0+tx_1,\qquad u=x_1-x_0,\qquad\mathcal L=\operatorname{mean}_{b,d}\left(v_\theta(x_t,t)-u\right)^2.$$

The conditional velocity u is the displacement between a pair of endpoints, but the network sees only the current position and time. Different endpoint pairs can reach the same position, so the network learns an average conditional velocity. Even an optimal network generally has nonzero training loss: irreducible variance is not an implementation error. See [Flow Matching Equations 5, 9, 22, and 23](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.02747v2) for gradient equivalence and linear conditional paths.

A point distribution is a special case: $v^*(x,t)=(\mu-x)/(1-t)$. Substituting the interpolated position gives a constant target velocity, zero oracle loss, and exact arrival at the data point in one Euler step. Marginal trajectories for general mixtures can curve, making multiple integration steps useful.

## 3. From equations to code

Implement three functions around the same training objective:

```text
interpolate: broadcast t [B] to [B,...] and construct the noise-to-data path
cfm_target: return the path’s derivative with respect to time
cfm_loss: evaluate model(x,t) at the result of interpolate
Average the squared elementwise error against cfm_target
```

`interpolate` and `cfm_target` preserve endpoint shape and dtype. `cfm_loss` returns a scalar, averages over the batch and every coordinate, and preserves gradients to model parameters.

`sample_t` and `euler_sample` are provided. The test harness manages the model, optimizer, and training loop, calling your `cfm_loss` during training. Time sampling is uniform by default; the helper’s logit-normal option is available for later comparison.

## 4. Conventions

| Item | This module’s convention |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoints | `x0` is noise; `x1` is data |
| Time | `t` has shape `[B]` and runs from 0 to 1 |
| Conditional path | The paper’s conditional OT path with zero terminal noise |
| Pairing | Independent noise and data |
| Loss reduction | Mean over the batch and every coordinate |
| Test model | `model(x,t)` returns a velocity with the same shape as x |

Regression against conditional targets learns the marginal velocity field, without solving an ODE for each training example.

## 5. Interactive visualizations

<viz id="flow_particles" />

Play the particle flow and move through time to inspect velocity arrows at current positions. Change Euler step counts to compare straight oracle paths with learned curved trajectories.

<viz id="convention_bug" />

Toggle the reversed-sampling bug to see the same model generate incorrect results. Compare the loss curve to understand why decreasing training loss alone does not establish correct sampling.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Further exploration

The supplied Euler solver integrates forward in time, evaluating at left endpoints to avoid the point oracle’s singularity at t=1:

$$x_{k+1}=x_k+\frac1n v_\theta(x_k,k/n),\quad k=0,\ldots,n-1.$$

For optional exploration, read [Rectified Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03003) on recoupling and [SD3 Equation 13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.03206v1) on reversed time conventions and nonuniform time sampling. These comparisons add no required functions to this module.
en.notes:
# Flow Matching: Review after passing

- Interpolation, target sign, and integration direction must agree. `test_point_zero_loss` checks training; `test_gaussian_transport` and `test_learns_eight_modes` check generation, rather than relying only on decreasing loss.
- The point-distribution oracle is singular at t=1. Euler evaluates left endpoints, so its largest evaluation time is (n-1)/n. `test_no_singular_endpoint` records the actual call times.
- Conditional targets have irreducible variance, so CFM loss generally cannot reach zero. Only the special point distribution in `test_point_zero_loss` has zero optimal error; the real training curves retain a nonzero final loss.
- The loss averages over every batch and coordinate element. Summing over coordinates before averaging over the batch differs by the number of dimensions. `test_reference` makes this contract explicit.
- A TimeMLP trained for 2,000 steps is not an exact oracle. The measured outlier fraction beyond radius .5 is .123; the specification's factor of 1.5 gives a threshold of .1845. MMD is calibrated by the same factor. Separately, all eight modes must be covered and each mode's share must be within .05 of .125. Environment details and measurements are in `problem.yaml`. These thresholds apply to a short training budget and do not imply the exact-oracle quality used in problem **8**.

The original exercise checked the time conventions against [Lipman Equations 22–23](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.02747v2), [Rectified Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03003), and [SD3 Equation 13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.03206v1) on 2026-10-13.
